claims.content: The Non-C2 JU wants to receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG, including track and Reference Point data, so that it can support its platform mission.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG, including track and Reference Point data, to support the platform mission.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: In one successful instance, the Non-C2 JU receives situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG containing the track and Reference Point data it needs for its platform mission.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Before the Non-C2 JU has received the situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG in this use case.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Non-C2 JU has received the situational awareness information (track and Reference Point data) from the Surveillance NPG.
in_scope_actions: Receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG
excluded_adjacent_actions: Transmission/sending of data by the Surveillance NPG
Using the received data to execute or support the platform mission
Separate monitoring activities beyond receiving the situational awareness data
variant_dimensions: Specific types of situational awareness data received: track data vs Reference Point data

claims.content: Non-C2 JU
The Non-C2 JU must be monitoring the Surveillance NPG to support its missions.
The availability of situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG—specifically remote surveillance track and point data in the J3 series messages—triggers the Non-C2 JU to receive it.
The Non-C2 JU monitors the Surveillance NPG for situational awareness information without transmitting on the Surveillance NPG.

The Non-C2 JU receives J3 series messages containing remote surveillance track and point data; simulated tracks, if received, retain their Simulation Indicator status unless explicitly dropped and re-reported.
The received situational awareness information includes track data and Reference Point data necessary to support the platform mission.
The received J3 messages include Force Tell and Emergency Indicators; when these indicators are set, they override all operator controllable data filters.
The remote surveillance track and point data provides the Non-C2 JU with situational awareness and early warning information.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of receiving live remote surveillance track data, the Non-C2 JU receives simulated tracks provided solely for training or test. The Simulation Indicator in the appropriate J3 message (and J2 message when applicable) is set to indicate the track is simulated. Simulated tracks must not be correlated with live tracks, and if both are displayed simultaneously, they must be readily distinguishable from each other.

Diverges from Step 2: If the Non-C2 JU receives a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, it automatically sets the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status. Exit: the specified track's designated mode(s) are placed in the No Data state; no change report is transmitted for a Valid-to-No-Data transition caused by this clearing function.

Diverges from Step 3: If a received track with Valid Data subsequently fails to respond to interrogations, the Non-C2 JU shall not change the track to the No Data status unless a Clear action is taken. Exit: the track remains in Valid Data status.

Diverges from Step 2: If the Non-C2 JU does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on a remote track, it must have the capability to automatically purge that track after a specific time interval. Exit: the track is purged.

Diverges from Step 2: If a specified time interval has elapsed since the remote track's/point's last report, the Non-C2 JU may automatically drop that track/point (purging). Exit: the track/point is dropped.

Diverges from Step 3: If the Non-C2 JU (as a NonR² JU) identifies an ID conflict and follows the inhibit-transmission action (ACT = 1), it must inhibit transmission of the J7.0 until the surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0. Exit: when the indicator value 0 is received, the inhibition condition is resolved.

Diverges from Step 3: If the Non-C2 JU (as a NonR² JU) identifies an ID conflict—including when the Identity Difference Indicator is set to value 1—it may take no action with respect to the reported ID; an operator alert may be provided as a system option. Exit: no action is taken on the reported ID.
The Non-C2 JU possesses situational awareness and early warning information derived from remote surveillance track and point data available in J3 series messages.

The Non-C2 JU holds the received remote track and Reference Point data in its local database; Force Tell and Emergency Alert indicators, if included in the received data, override operator-controllable filters.
If simulated tracks are received, they are maintained with unchanged Simulation Indicator status unless explicitly dropped and re-reported.
The received track and point data is reflected in the Non-C2 JU's surveillance data reporting state as updated track and point data.

inconsistency_hints: The preconditions slot claims the J3 track/point data must already be available, but the trigger is exactly that same availability. This collapses the preconditions and trigger into one event, so the use case has no distinct start. The required prior state that the Non-C2 JU is already monitoring/receiving on the Surveillance NPG is missing, which is why main flow step 1 opens with a monitoring action that actually belongs before the trigger.

The postconditions guarantee that simulated tracks are maintained with unchanged Simulation Indicator status unless explicitly dropped/re-reported, but the main flow contains no step addressing simulated tracks or Simulation Indicator handling, so the main flow does not lead to that postcondition.

citation_audit.description: Latest model-authored candidates after internal semantic grounding verification and DRA; aligned with delivered slots.
